thread:
addison: Heads-up: planning a batched reboot across us-west GPU pools to apply NIC fw + kernel micropatch. Window: Wed 2026-03-25 02:00–04:00 UTC. Expected impact: ~8–12% capacity dip per cohort; each node may evict jobs for up to ~90s while kdump/firmware completes. Canary = pool-a (5 nodes). Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8421
chao: Rollback criteria?
addison: If /v1/generate error rate spikes >2% OR p99 latency >800ms sustained for 5m -> pause run, roll nodes back to previous kernel/NIC fw, revert routing. See playbook link: https://go.redwood/ops/runbooks/inf-8421
ops_jun: Can we exclude Dedicated/reserved pools? tenant-acct-42 still needs pinned infra.
addison: Yes. We'll tag nodes with reserved=true and skip them in the cohort. Drains will skip pools with label redwood.reserved=true.
addison: Runbook drain snippet:
```
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=10m
kubectl uncordon <node>
```
sre-oncall-bot: :alarm_clock: Reminder set. I'll post a 'starting maintenance' notice 15m before the window and a 'finished' update after completion.
maria: FYI — customer impact: do retries from clients count as extra tokens? will billing reflect this?
finance_bot: For reserved capacity: no change. For hosted requests we expect a small bump in retry tokens in worst case; estimate $120–$350 in tail-case for the window based on last-month traffic patterns.
aj: I'll run a canary load fixture at 01:30 UTC (30% traffic) to validate p99 behavior before we start. CC @addison
addison: thanks — also enabling automatic fallback to comp-model-lite for routes if pool capacity drops below 80% so product stays online.
support_lead: Please add a customer-facing template. Support will stand up a priority thread if >50 tenants report errors. We'll monitor via support-sla dashboard.
addison: I'll update the runbook and post final comms. TL;DR: Wed 02:00 UTC, canary pool-a(5 nodes), exclude reserved pools, rollback if >2% errors or p99>800ms. :white_check_mark:
